Plant Energy Conversion

Overview:
Green organisms capture radiant energy from the sun and store it as chemical bonds inside sugar molecules.

Light Reactions:
Pigments in the thylakoid membrane absorb photons and split water, releasing oxygen as a byproduct.

Calvin Cycle:
Carbon dioxide from the air is fixed into organic compounds using energy carried by ATP and NADPH.

Chlorophyll:
This green pigment strongly reflects wavelengths in the middle of the visible spectrum.

Stomata:
Tiny pores on the leaf surface open and close to regulate gas exchange with the surrounding air.
